Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the

By means of this second bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant Manoj Kumar Gupta, who is involved in Case Crime No. 74 of 2022, under Section 376 IPC and Section 3/4 Prevention of Children from Sexual Offence Act, 2012, police station Phoolpur, district Varanasi,
seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text:
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected vide order dated 09.02.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 29666 of 2022 considering the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
Main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that the victim and informant have been examined as PW-1 and PW-2 before the trial Court but after cross-examination, victim has been declared hostile, therefore, there is bleak chance of conviction of the applicant.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 29666 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Lastly, it is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no chance of the applicant fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 20.02.2022 and in case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and cooperate with the trial.

On the other hand, learned A.G.A. for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that the victim and complainant (mother of the victim) in their examination-in-chief have supported the prosecution case making allegation of rape against the applicant but they have been won over from the side of the accused, therefore, they have given contradictory statements.
Hence, bail application of the applicant is liable to be rejected.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that examination-in-chief of the victim was recorded on 16.01.2023, in which she has supported the prosecution case but her cross-examination was done from the side of the accused on 22.02.2023,
therefore, she has given contradictory statement, as such, possibility of winning over of the victim from the side of the accused cannot be ruled out.
It is well settled that inference from the statement of any witness shall be drawn considering his/her statement in toto, not in isolation.
Hence, I do not find any good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail mainly on the ground that the victim has given contradictory statement in her cross-examination.
Accordingly, the bail application of the applicant is rejected.
It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.

However, the trial Court is directed to make an endeavour to conclude the trial expeditiously preferably within a period of nine months from the date of production of a copy of this order without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties strictly in accordance with the provisions of Section 309 Cr.P.C.
Order Date :- 16.1.2024
